narrative:
Your loan application was denied because the prediction estimated a 54.0% probability that you represent a bad credit risk. That is only slightly above a coin flip, but it is high enough to fall outside the bank’s acceptance range, so the application was not approved.

The strongest influence was your credit history. Your record shows no credits or all paid at the bank, while most approved applicants have existing paid credit (57.3%) and only about 1% share your exact history. Because it offers little evidence of successful borrowing and repayment, this was the top factor pushing toward bad credit. The second factor was your checking account status: a balance of 0–200 DM was the next strongest push toward bad risk; among approved applicants, such balances are much less common than having no checking account. The third factor worked in your favor: owning real estate was a positive sign, since about a third of approved applicants own property, but it was not enough to offset the first two concerns. Other details, such as requesting 1,778 DM against an approved average of about 3,020 DM, may look more moderate, but they did not outweigh the main concerns.

To improve your chances, focus on building a documented repayment history and, if possible, a stronger checking-account position. Ask the lender what records could be corrected, and consider reapplying after those areas improve or with a suitable guarantor or co-applicant.
